title: In 1947, operators found a literal bug in a computer: a moth
body: In 1947, operators of Harvard’s Mark II computer traced a fault to a moth trapped in a relay. They taped it into the logbook with the note “First actual case of bug being found.” The joke worked because engineers already called glitches “bugs”: Thomas Edison used the word in the 1870s. Grace Hopper, who worked on the machine, helped make the story famous.
